findings.section: Adjusted degradation in ep_loss relative to 30+ s
findings.claim: After controlling for phase, stakes, ply, material and the opponent's clock, a bullet clock under 5 s does not raise either side's ep_loss relative to 30+ s, and the player is not more susceptible than the opponents.
findings.metric: linear-model coefficient of the <5 s clock bucket on ep_loss relative to 30+ s, per side; difference is the side x clock interaction
findings.caveat: Linear adjustment for phase, stakes (ep_criticality / criticality buckets), ply, material and the opponent's clock; cannot remove residual selection into time pressure. The stakes control is strong: the clock's own effect lies between the models with and without it. ep_loss is calibrated with both clocks as features, so a blunder made with 2 s left costs fewer expected points than the same blunder with 30 s; cp_loss is clock-free.

findings.section: 7. What low-clock moves cost per game
findings.claim: Moves made with under 10 s cost the player 0.123 expected points per bullet game, the same as the opponents, about one seventh of all expected points the player gives away in bullet.
findings.metric: ep_loss summed over moves with clock_before < 10 s, per game, player vs opponents
findings.stake_note: Sum of ep_loss on the side's moves made with under 10 s, per game (zero when the side never got that low); an upper bound on what avoiding time pressure saves, since those moves would still carry some error, and the points lost by getting into time pressure are attributed to the earlier moves (Q4).
findings.caveat: ep_loss is calibrated with both clocks as features, so a blunder made with 2 s left costs fewer expected points than the same blunder with 30 s; cp_loss is clock-free.

findings.section: 8. What rating your low-clock play resembles
findings.claim: On the opponents' all-moves cp_loss-vs-rating curve, the player's bullet play under 10 s resembles a 775-rated player, against an actual mean rating of 932.
findings.metric: rating at which the opponents' move-weighted linear fit of cp_loss on pre-game rating equals the player's mean cp_loss on moves under 10 s
findings.caveat: Indicative only: opponents' pre-game rating is reconstructed (opponent_rating_after + my_rating_change), the cp_loss-rating slope is shallow (about -3 to -4 cp per 100 points) so intervals are wide by construction, and the player's low-clock moves (nearly all endgame) are compared to opponents' moves at all clocks and phases.

findings.caveat: Its rating equivalent is clipped to 0* [0*, 345] and is not carried here.

findings.section: 8. What rating your low-clock play resembles
findings.claim: Over all rapid moves the player's cp_loss resembles a 1151-rated player (actual mean rating 961); rapid has no low-clock cell with 30+ moves.
findings.metric: rating at which the opponents' fit of cp_loss on pre-game rating equals the player's mean cp_loss over all moves
findings.caveat: Indicative only: opponents' pre-game rating is reconstructed (opponent_rating_after + my_rating_change), the cp_loss-rating slope is shallow (about -3 to -4 cp per 100 points) so intervals are wide by construction, and the player's low-clock moves (nearly all endgame) are compared to opponents' moves at all clocks and phases.
